systems.label: Early visual
systems.description: Low-level vision: contrast, edges, color, and how much the picture changes. Rises with bright, busy, or fast-changing frames.

citations.text: Wandell BA, Dumoulin SO, Brewer AA (2007). Visual field maps in human cortex. Neuron 56:366-383. doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2007.10.012
Glasser MF et al. (2016). A multi-modal parcellation of human cerebral cortex. Nature 536:171-178. doi:10.1038/nature18933

systems.label: Motion
systems.description: The MT+ complex tracks visual motion: moving objects, camera moves, and optic flow.

citations.text: Huk AC, Dougherty RF, Heeger DJ (2002). Retinotopy and functional subdivision of human areas MT and MST. J Neurosci 22:7195-7205. doi:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.22-16-07195.2002
Glasser MF et al. (2016). A multi-modal parcellation of human cerebral cortex. Nature 536:171-178. doi:10.1038/nature18933

systems.label: Faces
systems.description: Fusiform face complex and posterior inferotemporal cortex, which respond most to faces and, more weakly, to bodies and objects.

citations.text: Kanwisher N, McDermott J, Chun MM (1997). The fusiform face area. J Neurosci 17:4302-4311. doi:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.17-11-04302.1997
Glasser MF et al. (2016). A multi-modal parcellation of human cerebral cortex. Nature 536:171-178. doi:10.1038/nature18933

systems.label: Places & scenes
systems.description: Parahippocampal and retrosplenial areas that respond to places, landscapes, and spatial layout.

citations.text: Epstein R, Kanwisher N (1998). A cortical representation of the local visual environment. Nature 392:598-601. doi:10.1038/33402
Glasser MF et al. (2016). A multi-modal parcellation of human cerebral cortex. Nature 536:171-178. doi:10.1038/nature18933

systems.label: Sound
systems.description: Early auditory cortex: loudness, pitch, and acoustic change in music, voice, and effects.

citations.text: Moerel M, De Martino F, Formisano E (2014). An anatomical and functional topography of human auditory cortical areas. Front Neurosci 8:225. doi:10.3389/fnins.2014.00225
Glasser MF et al. (2016). A multi-modal parcellation of human cerebral cortex. Nature 536:171-178. doi:10.1038/nature18933

systems.label: Speech & language
systems.description: Superior temporal and inferior frontal language areas. They follow spoken words and, more strongly, meaningful sentences.

citations.text: Fedorenko E et al. (2010). New method for fMRI investigations of language. J Neurophysiol 104:1177-1194. doi:10.1152/jn.00032.2010
Glasser MF et al. (2016). A multi-modal parcellation of human cerebral cortex. Nature 536:171-178. doi:10.1038/nature18933

systems.label: Social cognition
systems.description: Temporo-parietal junction, temporal pole, and medial cortex, linked to thinking about people's intentions and stories.

citations.text: Saxe R, Kanwisher N (2003). People thinking about thinking people: the role of the temporo-parietal junction in "theory of mind". NeuroImage 19:1835-1842. doi:10.1016/S1053-8119(03)00230-1
Glasser MF et al. (2016). A multi-modal parcellation of human cerebral cortex. Nature 536:171-178. doi:10.1038/nature18933

systems.label: Attention
systems.description: Dorsal attention network (frontal eye fields and intraparietal sulcus), engaged when the viewer orients to and tracks what is on screen.

citations.text: Corbetta M, Shulman GL (2002). Control of goal-directed and stimulus-driven attention in the brain. Nat Rev Neurosci 3:201-215. doi:10.1038/nrn755
Glasser MF et al. (2016). A multi-modal parcellation of human cerebral cortex. Nature 536:171-178. doi:10.1038/nature18933

systems.label: Salience
systems.description: Anterior insula and dorsal anterior cingulate, which respond to surprising, important, or emotionally charged moments.

citations.text: Seeley WW et al. (2007). Dissociable intrinsic connectivity networks for salience processing and executive control. J Neurosci 27:2349-2356. doi:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.5587-06.2007
Glasser MF et al. (2016). A multi-modal parcellation of human cerebral cortex. Nature 536:171-178. doi:10.1038/nature18933

systems.label: Valuation
systems.description: Ventromedial prefrontal and orbitofrontal cortex, associated with subjective value. The least reliable system: fMRI signal here is weak.

citations.text: Bartra O, McGuire JT, Kable JW (2013). The valuation system: a coordinate-based meta-analysis of BOLD fMRI experiments examining neural correlates of subjective value. NeuroImage 76:412-427. doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2013.02.063
Glasser MF et al. (2016). A multi-modal parcellation of human cerebral cortex. Nature 536:171-178. doi:10.1038/nature18933
